- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict sharp declines; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- After a price spike (e.g., >75), model often overreacts with sustained overforecasting; cap forecast at +2% above peak for 5–7 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) and price drops >5% from recent high, model fails to anticipate further decline; add 1–2% downward bias for next 7 days.
- Model consistently underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if 30d forecast is >70.5 and sentiment neutral, reduce by 1–2% for next 10 days.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model overfits short-term noise; smooth 30d forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ true values.
- If true outcome shows “double dip” (e.g., drop then rebound), model often misses second leg; add 0.5–1% upward bias for 3–5 days after rebound.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is negative and price is below 65, model tends to overcorrect upward; cap forecast at 68–70 unless sentiment turns strongly positive.
